title: Real machine admission fixture
summary: The setup operation fixture.machine-admission-prepare runs the installed candidate's own machine_qa_admission_host on the test machine, so the exact candidate serves admission journeys. Modes self-hosted and self-hosted-company-sign-in boot the unchanged self-host server entrypoint on loopback (ports 19121 and 19122) with YOKE_SERVER_MODE=self-host as the bundle sets it against a disposable embedded Postgres; the real first boot creates the Fixture Owner and saves the owner's token owner-only with an approver config the person uses through YOKE_MACHINE_HOME. Company sign-in adds a disposable stub provider whose only identity is the teammate, after the owner runs yoke invite EMAIL --role operator (an email invite without a role grants none). Mode local runs the real yoke init --local in a fixture-only machine home. The fixture never approves, invites a machine or redeems anything. The post-state assertion fixture.machine-admission-state-assert compares people, machines, active credentials, linked identities and consumed teammate invites (exactly one, consumed by the new machine, on self-hosted) and the teammate's org role with the baseline recorded at start (owner-admitted, teammate-admitted or nothing-admitted) and fails as machine_admission_state_mismatch with the changed rows. Start and cleanup refusals keep their named reason in the operation row; cleanup is registered before start and retries when it fails.
